images.caption: Figure 1:Scale, diversity, and downstream impact of synthesized Cowork environments.Left:Our environment-synthesis pipeline produces 64.9K tasks across 14 top-level scenarios, with representative workspaces illustrating diverse personal and professional workflows.Right:The leaderboard demonstrates the effectiveness of training on these environments: Ours-27B ranks second across six agentic benchmarks and achieves the highest average scores on PawBench and ClawEval among the evaluated models.

Figure 2:Cowork environment packaging and rollout.(a) Each environment is represented as a Harbor-compatible task package augmented with a user simulator, bundling the task instruction, runtime, reference solution, verifier, and user profiles.
(b) During rollout, the user simulator communicates with the acting agent. It also observes and edits the shared workspace state in response to the agent’s progress.
(c) The resulting trajectory records user messages, agent actions, and tool observations; the hybrid verifier then evaluates it.

Figure 3:Overview of Cowork environment synthesis and agent training.Left:Environment synthesis starts with(a)Task Specification(Section3.1) and proceeds through(b)theBuild–Execute–Reviseloop (Section3.2).Right:(c)Trajectory Generationwith stateful user simulation is followed by(d)Filtering(Section3.4).Bottom:The resulting environments and trajectories support agent training with SFT, RL, and OPD.

Figure 4:Cowork environment synthesis and stateful user simulation.Left:The interaction loop among user, agent, and the environment in the real world.Right:Theuser simulatorruns outside the acting-agent sandbox and conditions each intervention on private user state and current task progress. The.user/directory stores persistent context;.patch/provides turn-specific behavioral instructions and authorized workspace updates. The acting agent observes only public messages and the resulting changes(Section3.3).
Figure 6:ClawEval performance of Ours-9B, Ours-27B, and Ours-35B-A3B over supervised training, with progress normalized to the final checkpoint.
Figure 7:Agentic transfer and general-capability retention under OPD. Dashed lines mark SFT teacher performance; exposure is normalized to the final checkpoint.
